rules.title: Simultaneous Playthrough
rules.shortSummary: Both players must playthrough the games simultaneously.

versions.description: The two players play through the same game simultaneously.

Encounters for players on each route are linked. If one player fails to catch their encounter for a route, the other player must box or release their encounter for that route as well. If both players successfully catch their first encounter for the route, those two Pokémon are “linked” as partners.

rules.title: Pokemon Dying
rules.shortSummary: When a pokemon dies, it's partner dies as well.

versions.description: When one player’s Pokémon faints, its partner on the other player’s team must be boxed or released as well.
If a Pokémon is placed in the PC, its partner on the other player’s team must be placed in the PC as well.

rules.title: Restricted Typings
rules.shortSummary: No sharing of the same primary typing.

versions.description: Often, players will restrict the use of shared types between the teams, meaning that no Pokémon on either team may share the same primary type.

rules.title: Randomized Encounters
rules.shortSummary: Pokemon are randomized to promote variety!

versions.description: It’s common to randomize the encounters on each route for this challenge, to promote greater Pokémon and type variety between the teams, especially on early routes where Pokémon selection is limited.
Only the first wild Pokémon encountered in a route or area can be caught. If the player fails to catch it (ie. it flees or faints), their opportunity to catch a Pokémon in that area is lost.
The player must nickname all Pokémon they catch or obtain.

rules.title: Duplicate Clause
rules.shortSummary: To prevent duplicates, and promote variety!

versions.description: If the first Pokémon in an area is one the player already owns, they may continue battling until they encounter one they do not own, and then attempt to catch it. This rule prevents a player from having multiples of the same Pokémon, especially early in the game when the selection of different Pokémon on the first few routes is limited.
If the player encounters a shiny wild Pokémon, they may catch it, even if a wild Pokémon has already been encountered in that area. This does not count as the encounter for that area.
